title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Avery Chen
summary: Comprehensive company handbook covering what it's like to work at Redwood, our role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks summary, hiring and onboarding overview, and the primary internal tools every employee should know.
content:
Overview

Redwood is a developer-first inference platform focused on production-grade LLM serving. This handbook page provides a single-page reference for new and existing employees: who we are, how teams are organized, the career progression framework, benefits and perks, the typical hiring and onboarding lifecycle, and the primary internal tools and how to get started with them.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & expectations

- Mission alignment: Ship reliable, cost-efficient LLM inference for customers. We expect engineers and cross-functional partners to prioritize reliability, observability, and measurable cost/latency improvements.
- Principles: Customer-first reliability, pragmatic experimentation, data-informed decisions, and clear ownership.
- Ways of working: asynchronous-first communication, weekly team-level standups, quarterly planning and OKRs, and biannual 1:1 calibration for managers.

2) Roles & career ladders (high-level)

We use a role + level system to set expectations and evaluate growth. Below are the most common individual contributor (IC) ladders; equivalent manager ladders exist for people managers. For specifics consult your manager and the People Ops compensation packet.

| Function | Typical titles (IC) | Leveling focus |
|---------|---------------------|----------------|
| Engineering (Infra/Serving/Platform) | Software Engineer I–III, Senior, Staff, Principal | Delivery of service-level features, system design, reliability improvements, cross-team impact |
| Product | Associate PM, PM, Senior PM, Lead PM | Product discovery, roadmap ownership, cross-functional outcomes, feature success metrics |
| Research/Applied ML | ML Engineer, Research Engineer, Senior Research Engineer | Model quality, evals, reproducible benchmarks, model onboarding to serving |
| SRE/Operations | SRE I–III, Senior SRE, Staff SRE | SLO ownership, incident leadership, capacity planning, runbook quality |

Career ladder signals and expectations (summary):
- IC Levels: I–III emphasize execution and domain knowledge; Senior–Principal emphasize cross-team influence, architecture, and mentoring.
- Promotion evidence: sustained impact on product metrics, demonstrated system ownership, well-documented design reviews, and mentorship of others.
- Manager progression: people managers are evaluated on team outcomes, hiring and retention, development of reports, and cross-team collaboration.

3) Benefits & perks (employee-facing summary)

Redwood's benefits are designed to be competitive and supportive of diverse needs. Below is a summary — full policy docs live in People Ops.

Health & wellness:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution tiers for full-time employees. Domestic partners covered.
- Health savings account (HSA) with employer contribution for eligible plans.
- Mental health: 12 sessions/year covered through the EAP plus subsidized therapy stipend.

Financial & time-off:
- Competitive base salary + equity grants at hire, with annual review cycles.
- Parental leave: primary and secondary caregiver policies (see People Ops for durations and eligibility).
- PTO: Flexible vacation policy with recommended minimum of 15 days/year; 10 sick days. Company-wide holidays plus winter break.
- 401(k) or regional equivalent with company matching where available.

Development & family support:
- Learning & development stipend per year for conferences, training, and books.
- Home office stipend for remote hires and relocation support for certain roles.
- Commuter benefits and flexible work arrangements depending on team needs.

Perks and culture budget:
- Team-level offsites (annually), monthly team socials, and volunteer match program.
- Hardware & software budget: employees receive approved laptops and accessories; provision process is in the Internal Tools section below.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy:
- We hire for mission fit, technical ability, and demonstrated ownership. Interviews assess past impact, problem solving, system design (for engineering), and cross-functional communication.
- Diverse hiring: interview panels must include diverse representation. Interview feedback uses standardized scorecards.

Recruiting lifecycle (high-level):
1. Requisition opened by hiring manager and approved by People Ops + Finance (template: hiring-requisition).
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter screens candidates; hiring manager reviews qualified screens.
3. Onsite/loop: Standardized loop with technical exercise, system design or case study, and cross-functional partner interview.
4. Decision & offer: Hiring manager gathers panel feedback; People Ops owns compensation and offer letter.
5. Acceptance, background check (as required), and start date scheduling.

New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days) — mandatory steps:
1. Before day 1:
   - Confirm offer & paperwork with People Ops.
   - Complete IT account provisioning request (link on Internal Tools page).
2. Day 1
   - Welcome orientation with People Ops and Engineering orientation for technical hires.
   - Set up laptop, MFA, SSO, Slack, email, and access to the main Redwood Confluence and GitHub org.
3. Week 1
   - Meet your manager for goals & 30/60/90 plan.
   - Join team standups and shadow on-call rotations where relevant.
   - Complete security training and code-of-conduct acknowledgment.
4. 30 days
   - Deliver first small scoped task (bug fix or doc) to validate environment and codebase familiarity.
   - One-on-one with manager to calibrate onboarding progress.
5. 60 days
   - Take ownership of a medium-sized deliverable and lead a design review.
6. 90 days
   - Deliver measurable impact, present a 90-day summary to manager and mentor, and agree on next objectives.

Manager checklist for onboarding:
- Assign onboarding buddy and schedule weekly touchpoints.
- Create clear success metrics for 30/60/90 days.
- Enable access to required repos, dashboards, and services.

5) Internal tools & how to get started

This section lists the core internal tools used at Redwood, the primary owner, and quick start steps. Detailed runbooks and access links are maintained in team wikis.

- Identity & Access (SSO/Okta) — Owner: Security & IT
  - Purpose: Central login, SSO, MFA.
  - Quickstart: Accept Okta invite, enroll MFA, join Redwood directory groups. For elevated access request, open an IR ticket.

- GitHub (org: redwood-inference) — Owner: Eng DevEx
  - Purpose: Code hosting, PRs, and CODEOWNERS.
  - Quickstart: Join org via invite, set up SSH keys, read CODEOWNERS and contributing.md, complete required repo-level access request form.

- CI/CD (Buildkite + Terraform Cloud) — Owner: Eng Infra
  - Purpose: Pipelines for builds, deploys, and IaC runs.
  - Quickstart: Ensure GitHub integration, sign in to Buildkite, and review team pipelines. For Terraform apply permissions, file an access request with owner_team=eng-infra.

- Observability & Dashboards (Datadog + Tempo + Loki) — Owner: Eng Platform
  - Purpose: Metrics, traces, logs, and SLO dashboards.
  - Quickstart: Request dashboard read access, review team SLO dashboards, and subscribe to oncall rotation.

- Confluence (internal docs) — Owner: Eng DevEx / People Ops
  - Purpose: Company documentation, runbooks, and handbooks.
  - Quickstart: Request edit access for your team space, complete Confluence writing guidelines, and add yourself as the document owner for new pages you create.

- Incident & Pager (PagerDuty) — Owner: Eng SRE
  - Purpose: On-call scheduling and incident management.
  - Quickstart: Complete incident training, sign up for on-call shadowing, and confirm paging limits and escalation policies.

- HR/People Platform (Workday / Rippling) — Owner: People Ops
  - Purpose: Payroll, benefits enrollment, and time off.
  - Quickstart: Complete profile, enroll in benefits during the onboarding window, and add emergency contact.

- Finance & Expense (Brex or Expensify) — Owner: Finance
  - Purpose: Company cards, expense reports, and vendor payments.
  - Quickstart: Request company card via Finance, submit first expense with receipts and project codes.

- Customer & Product Feedback (Gainsight or Canny) — Owner: Product / CS
  - Purpose: Customer feature requests, product usage insights.
  - Quickstart: Join product channel, file triage tickets for customer escalations, and tag relevant product owners.

6) Promotions, performance reviews & compensation cadence

- Review cadence: Annual performance reviews with mid-year check-ins. Compensation adjustments typically follow annual review cycles; promotions are considered on demonstrated impact and role readiness.
- Promotion process: Candidate prepares a promotion packet with accomplishments, 360 feedback, and a manager endorsement. People Ops coordinates calibration across teams.

7) Offboarding & transfers

- Standard offboarding checklist: manager initiates offboarding in People Ops system, revoke access to SSO, return hardware, knowledge transfer doc, and finalize payroll/benefits.
- Internal transfers: Employees are encouraged to apply to internal roles; managers should approve shadowing and provide references.

8) Useful links and contacts

- People Ops: people-ops@redwoodinfra.internal
- IT/Security support: it-support@redwoodinfra.internal
- Eng DevEx & GitHub access: devex@redwoodinfra.internal
- Oncall & Incident: oncall-ops@redwoodinfra.internal

Appendix: Templates & example artifacts

- 30/60/90 plan template: (link in Confluence templates space)
- Hiring requisition template: hiring-requisition (People Ops template)
- Promotion packet checklist: promotion-checklist (People Ops)
- New hire tech setup script example (bash):

  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -e
  # Install dev tools
  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y build-essential curl git
  # Configure git
  git config --global user.name "Your Name"
  git config --global user.email "you@redwoodinfra.internal"
  # Clone starter repo
  git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/starter-kit.git ~/starter-kit

Contributing and questions

If you find outdated information on this page, please open a Confluence edit request or contact People Ops. For role-specific questions, reach out to your manager or the listed owner teams above.
